newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana exchange cuts settlement time, shares firmer.
newsitem.headline: Ghana exchange cuts settlement time, shares firmer.

text.p: Ghana's stock exchange cut its clearing and settlement period on Friday from 10 working days to five, but investors remained cautious in the run up to next month's national elections, dealers said.
The GSE All-Share Index rose 0.29 points to 367.55 points in Friday trading from 367.26 on Wednesday.

The index made one of its biggest one-day gains in recent trading on Wednesday, jumping 1.68 points from Monday's 365.58. Shares traded on Friday fell to 77,710 from Wednesday's 348,190. On Monday a modest 11,530 were traded.
Shares offered on Friday fell to 868,450 from 1.49 million on Wednesday. Demand fell to 213,450 from 533,530.

Earlier, the exchange said in a statement that it had established a new clearing and settlement house and the clearing and settlement period for any transaction on its trading floor would fall to five working days from November 1.
Stock brokers and registrars of listed companies previously handled clearing and settlement.

The reform would also apply to over-the-counter trade outside the Monday, Wednesday and Friday trading sessions, it said. This is limited to shares in market heavyweight Ashanti Goldfields Company. ($=1,720 cedis)
